summary: Material changes since the prior snapshot: visible Hormuz traffic improved to 10 commodity-vessel transits on September 23 but remained below its recent average and dramatically below pre-war normal; U.S.-Iran diplomacy still showed no concrete progress and oil's intraday risk premium rose. USD/TWD closed at 31.780 on September 24. Taiwan approved a 2027 minimum monthly wage of NT$30,900, subject to the normal approval/effective process. The Trump-Xi summit was still in progress at this cutoff, so no summit outcome was inferred. No new CPI/PCE/NFP/ISM, Taiwan PMI/exports/export-orders/leading-indicator/central-bank decision, or China PMI release was found.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: Taiwan external demand remains strong, but a weaker TWD, high U.S. yields and persistent oil/freight risk create mixed effects: exporters gain FX translation support while importers, airlines, petrochemical users and duration-sensitive growth equities face cost or valuation headwinds.

key_drivers.name: Hormuz remains severely impaired despite daily traffic rebound
key_drivers.observed: Reuters-linked preliminary tracking showed 10 commodity-vessel transits on September 23 versus 7 a day earlier, below the roughly 17-vessel 10-day average and far below roughly 125 large commercial vessels/day before the war.
key_drivers.interpretation: The daily rebound is not normalization; energy, LNG and freight tail risks remain elevated, with AIS-dark traffic an important measurement caveat.

key_drivers.name: Oil risk premium rises as U.S.-Iran talks lack concrete progress
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported Brent $105.51/bbl and WTI $93.90/bbl at 09:40 GMT September 24 while U.S.-Iran positions remained divided.
key_drivers.interpretation: Persistent oil risk raises inflation, freight and input-cost pressure for Taiwan while supporting energy-linked pricing power.

key_drivers.name: Taiwan dollar weakens
key_drivers.observed: USD/TWD closed at 31.780 on September 24, up NT$0.064 from the prior close.
key_drivers.interpretation: A weaker TWD can support exporter translation but raises imported energy and commodity costs.

key_risks: Hormuz traffic remains far below normal despite a one-day rebound.
U.S.-Iran talks have not produced concrete progress and oil risk premium remains elevated.
U.S. long yields remain a valuation headwind after the 10Y closed above 5% on September 23.
Trump-Xi summit outcome was not yet verified at cutoff; Taiwan arms, technology and trade issues remain event risks.
DXY, VIX and copper lack fresh authoritative closes in this snapshot.

policy_tone.fed: Restrictive/hawkish after the September 16 decision; no newer decision incorporated.
policy_tone.taiwan_central_bank: Hold at 2.0% with selective credit easing.
policy_tone.china: September LPR unchanged; no new PMI release.
policy_tone.us_china: Busan trade arrangement extension reduces near-term tariff risk, but summit outcome was still pending at cutoff.
policy_tone.middle_east: Diplomacy remains active without concrete convergence; physical Hormuz traffic remains severely impaired.
policy_tone.global: Restrictive financial conditions plus elevated energy/security risk.
